verification.algebra: Setting the gradient of Eq5 to zero gives (Phi Phi^T + lambda m I) w = Phi y with Phi = sigma(F_hat X^T)/sqrt(k): exactly notebook cell7. Using the literal Eq6 as the objective would give (Phi Phi^T + lambda I) w = Phi y, i.e. effective ridge lambda/m. Eq6 data term = m x Eq5 data term, penalty unchanged, so Eq6 != m*Eq5.

issue_adjudication.decision: Estimator: the second layer is DEFINED by Eq5 (half mean squared residual + (lambda/2)||w||^2, lambda=1e-4 in the Fig1b configuration); the task will state this formula and the resulting normal equation. Reported training metric: the task will call the notebook quantity 'Eq5 objective value at w_hat' and will name Eq6 separately as printed; it will not call either the training error without the formula. Because a literal Eq6 grows linearly in m, it cannot have the finite proportional limit asserted in Thm3/4(i); this is recorded as an apparent notation inconsistency in v1, NOT an adjudicated author typo. Conservative spec: training error reported as the normalized Eq5 objective, with Eq6 literal given only as a note.
issue_adjudication.classification: resolved_for_task_spec; author intent for Eq6 not determined

issue_adjudication.decision: Task metric = Eq7 MSE, estimated on fresh held-out samples drawn from the same Eq2 mixture; the task will state that the author notebook's plotted 'generalization error' is half of an empirical test MSE (factor exactly 1/2 on the same sample), so absolute values in Figure 1(b) correspond to half-MSE if the notebook produced that figure. Positive rescaling preserves orderings/signs of paired differences and ratios but changes absolute values/thresholds; any comparison with reported numbers must convert units explicitly. A finite-sample test MSE is an estimate, not the population expectation.

issue_adjudication.decision: Task uses two distinct names: max_hermite_degree D (=3 for the Fig1b configuration) and theorem index l = D+1 (=4), and states the beta interval in terms of l. The Figure1 caption's 'l=5' is recorded as an unresolved caption/notation discrepancy (it could be a cap across panels or use a different index convention); it is not used to override the code-and-theorem-consistent D=3/l=4 choice. Coefficient normalization (h_j vs h_j/j!) and probabilists' Hermite polynomials must be stated.

evidence.notebook_cell13: NN(w, F, dataF, data, data_new, ReLU, ReLU_prime, relu_hermite, eta) -> gradient step uses activationF/derivative = original; features = activation(F_hat@X.T) uses Hermite surrogate
evidence.notebook_cell10: act_func(x) = hermeval(x/b, h) + hs * randn(*x.shape) (fresh noise per element per call)

issue_adjudication.decision: Task fixes: (1) F_hat is computed ONCE with the original activation sigma and sigma' (Eq3-4); (2) the NN model and the Hermite model share the same F, w, first-stage data and F_hat and differ only in the activation used to build ridge features and test predictions; (3) the residual Gaussian term h*_l z is part of the surrogate, drawn independently per hidden unit and per sample (independent for train and test features), not an optional truncation detail; (4) b = sqrt(n/Tr(Sigma)) uses the population trace, not the empirical norm of F_hat x. Training the first layer with the surrogate, or dropping the noise term, would change the method and is not allowed as 'the Hermite model'. Point (3) per-element independence is the notebook's reading of Eq16 (paper writes a scalar z); it is recorded as the adopted interpretation.
issue_adjudication.classification: resolved_for_task_spec; per-element noise independence = interpretation consistent with notebook

evidence.notebook_cell9: theta1[:d] = n**(beta*(1-alpha)) (same for component 2); xi normalized by sqrt(||Sigma||_2)*||xi|| with Sigma = 0.5*Sigma1 + 0.5*Sigma2

issue_adjudication.decision: Paper fixes only asymptotic orders, so the task must give concrete constants: theta_{c,1} = n^{beta(1-alpha)} for both components, eta = n^{beta alpha}, A.5 constant C=1 w.r.t. the mixture covariance. With two nearly orthogonal rank-one spikes and rho=0.5, ||Sigma|| ≈ 1 + theta/2, so eta*||Sigma|| ≈ 0.59 n^beta at n=1000, alpha≈0.53 — consistent with ≍ but not equality; the task must not describe eta*||Sigma|| as exactly n^beta. At alpha=1 theta=1, not 0.

cpu_smoke.implementation_note: Independent NumPy float64 implementation from Eq2-7, A.3-A.6, Eq16. Follows notebook for concrete constants (eta, theta, xi normalization, test size 5m, lambda, D=3, quadrature with 100 probabilists' Gauss-Hermite nodes). Differences from notebook: NumPy instead of JAX; numpy QR instead of scipy; ||Sigma|| via eigvalsh instead of SVD norm; i.i.d. component sampling; own RNG stream. Per-fit timing recomputes nothing extra: first-layer step is timed once per activation per trial but charged to both nn and hermite fits (notebook recomputes the step for each of its 6 NN() calls, so this matches notebook cost).
cpu_smoke.docker_command: docker run --rm --network none --cpus 2 --memory 2g --pids-limit 128 --read-only --tmpfs /tmp --user 10001:10001 -e OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=2 -v <gaussian_cpu_smoke>:/smoke:ro mrhbench-pilot/iv:860c335d9324 python /smoke/smoke.py '{"seed": ...}'
cpu_smoke.sanity_numbers_not_findings: At this single config NN and Hermite test half-MSE were close for all three activations in all 3 runs (e.g. run1 trial0 relu 0.0263 vs 0.0258). Recorded only as implementation sanity, NOT as validation of the paper's findings.

extrapolation_labelled.label: EXTRAPOLATION from one configuration; not measured
extrapolation_labelled.formula: 20 alpha x (setup + 20 trials x 6 fits x per_fit)
extrapolation_labelled.assumptions: Per-fit cost independent of alpha (flop count unchanged; only constants change); same host, 2 CPUs quota, OpenBLAS 2 threads; excludes container start (~0.5 s observed), JAX dispatch/compile overhead of the original notebook, plotting, and any LLM-agent thinking/tool time.
extrapolation_labelled.interpretation: Full notebook-scale sweep on this host would take on the order of 15 minutes of pure compute in the 2-CPU/2GiB envelope, peak RSS ~0.46 GiB. This supports CPU feasibility in principle; it does not set the package budget or the solver's design (grids/repeats are solver choices), and a solver spending its wall-clock on multiple exploratory sweeps could exceed a 1200 s budget.

host.note: --cpus is a CFS quota; container still sees 20 CPUs, hence OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=2 was set explicitly. Timings depend on host/virtualization.
